general.temas: The election debate between Sánchez and Feijóo and the polls ahead of the November 29 election dominate several front pages. Also recurring are Puigdemont’s remarks, the summit of Trump, Putin and Xi, Cintia Rocho’s request for police protection and the ATP Finals. Only ABC highlights the International Court of Justice’s ruling against Myanmar for genocide against the Rohingya.
general.motivo_crispacion: The election campaign accounts for much of the tension, with Sánchez and Feijóo preparing for a debate described in some headlines in combative terms. Puigdemont’s remarks prompt accusations against Sánchez from the PP and a legal complaint from Vox, while other headlines report recriminations and insults between political opponents. There are also reports of alleged scandals and conflict in classrooms. Sport, special offers, and cultural and educational stories provide less contentious subjects.

El País.resumen:
- Sánchez and Feijóo prepare for a head-to-head election debate, with the PP two points ahead of the PSOE in a poll.
- An election analysis links abstention to neighbourhood income levels.
- The front page covers a dispute between Delgado and Ayuso, questions an allegation circulated by Alvise and features an interview with Ada Colau.
- Xi, Trump and Putin pledge to push for UN reform and ensure energy stability.
- Other stories cover public housing and Blackstone, reactions to an interview with Sánchez, and accounts from Tamar Novas and Camila Gutiérrez.
El País.motivo_populismo: Straight news headlines predominate, although phrases such as “the first big hoax of the campaign falls apart” and “pulled his strings” add drama, and insults such as “coward” are highlighted in quoted remarks.
El País.sesgo: The selection gives priority to the election campaign and highlights content critical of Ayuso, Alvise and Blackstone, alongside interviews with voices expressing left-wing positions. The coverage also pays attention to income inequality and public housing.

El Mundo.resumen:
- Puigdemont discusses his negotiations with the PSOE; the PP and Vox respond with criticism and a legal complaint.
- The PSOE and the PP disagree over whether to include corruption in the election debate.
- A poll shows the PP and Vox retaining their majority, with 14.3% of voters undecided; another story examines differences in voting between men and women.
- Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping meet in China; police examine the use of flotation devices by people swimming into Ceuta.
- Stories cover threats in the Cloacas case, school conflicts, Alcaraz’s health and the search for a galleon.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Confrontational or sensationalist phrases stand out, including “defeat Spain”, “for a seat of power”, “war of the sexes” and “gobble up 800,000 votes”, although several appear as quotations and other headlines maintain a straight-news tone.
El Mundo.sesgo: The selection highlights stories and statements critical of Sánchez and the PSOE, particularly in relation to Puigdemont and corruption, without including a response from the PSOE in these headlines. It also gives prominence to the positions of the PP and Vox.

ABC.resumen:
- The November 29 campaign and the debate between Sánchez and Feijóo are the focus of the front page.
- Redondo announces that he will not vote for Sánchez and criticises his ambition.
- The Transport Ministry paid for cancer treatment for Ábalos’s ex-wife; Cintia Rocho requests police protection to testify in the “Cloacas” case.
- The International Court of Justice finds that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.
- There are also sports stories, things to do in Madrid, Black Friday offers and election tools.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Phrases such as “a rematch of the 2023 disaster” and “only victory will do” dramatise the political contest, although there is no apparent explicit appeal to the people against the elites.
ABC.sesgo: The selection and wording present several stories unfavourable to the PSOE and Sánchez, while Feijóo is associated with “absolute calm”. The campaign coverage highlights rivalry and electoral pressure.

Público.resumen:
- The debate between Sánchez and Feijóo is portrayed as marked by confrontation and pressure on both men.
- The campaign is presented as a personal matter for Sánchez, while Puigdemont enters the fray.
- Frente Amplio proposes changes to regional financing and criticises Ayuso’s tax policy.
- Feijóo’s housing pledge and the PP and Vox’s tax cuts are questioned.
- Other prominent stories include the abolition of an Equality and Migration department and the use of AI in the campaign.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “mud-slinging”, “Vietnam”, “fiasco” and “the art of insulting” add drama and disparagement, although other headlines maintain a straight-news tone.
Público.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach critical of the PP, Vox and some of their proposals, particularly on housing and taxation. There are also headlines critical of Sánchez and Junts.

OKdiario.resumen:
- Rafa Jódar plays Ben Shelton at the ATP Finals and loses the first set.
- An Indian student creates an app to correct hand tremors when drawing.
- An investor warns that retirement will cease to exist.
- Hernández de Cos has secured the support needed to lead the ECB, according to Expansión.
- The front page includes stories on archaeology, business, travel, pets and entertainment.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: The alarmist tone of “retirement is going to cease to exist” and sensationalist phrases such as “archaeologists can’t believe it” stand out, without an explicit appeal to the people against the elites.
OKdiario.sesgo: The selection favours practical-interest, entertainment and business content, with some eye-catching headlines. No clear political bias is apparent.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see two overlapping campaigns. One revolves around the head-to-head debate and who scores points; the other is playing out in neighbourhoods where, according to election data, fewer people vote than in higher-income areas. I don’t think that inequality can be separated from the class struggle: a democracy in which the working-class voice carries less weight leaves more room for the power of money.

The case of the tenant who waited ten years for public housing until Blackstone intervened illustrates an intolerable priority: access to a right should not depend on the influence of a fund. I support a large stock of democratically managed public and collective housing, as opposed to the logic of profit. And I reject tax cuts that weaken funding for healthcare, education and the other services that sustain our shared life.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I see how the election debate turns politics into a competition between leaders, while abstention is higher in low-income neighbourhoods. I won’t assume that those who don’t vote think like me, but I do question a system that reduces participation to choosing who will rule for the next few years.

The story of the tenant who waited ten years for public housing and obtained it after Blackstone spoke to a Madrid official reveals something troubling: economic power can open doors that remain closed to everyone else. I don’t want to replace that dependence with obedience to another party. I prefer to organise from the bottom up, through assemblies, mutual aid and collective management of resources, without letting the state or property owners decide for us. Individual freedom needs communities capable of sustaining it.
opiniones.liberal:
The head-to-head debate deserves to be more than a competition for the tactical vote. I want to know how much the candidates plan to spend, how they will fund their promises and which taxes they are willing to cut. The tax cuts proposed by the PP and Vox will only be responsible if they come with clear priorities and spending controls: passing the bill on to the future is not liberalism.

Nor do I agree with Frente Amplio’s proposal to prevent what it calls regional “tax dumping”. Competition between administrations can give citizens options and force governments to justify what they charge. On housing, the story about Blackstone and a tenant reinforces my conviction that public decisions must follow transparent rules, not depend on influence. A limited state, subject to checks, better protects freedom and demands accountability from both governments and citizens.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I have no interest in seeing today’s debate become a contest of gestures and advisers. I want to know what the candidates are willing to do to defend Spain’s unity. Puigdemont’s remarks about his negotiations with the PSOE demand clear explanations: national sovereignty cannot be treated as a bargaining chip for forming a government.

I also expect answers about Ceuta. If police find that the flotation devices used by people swimming into the city were distributed according to a prearranged plan, the state must investigate and strengthen border controls. A strict immigration policy, applied with respect for the law and human dignity, is an obligation of any responsible government.

And while the campaign revolves around the leaders’ image, conflict in classrooms is increasing. I support teachers’ authority and an education that instils responsibility and respect.
opiniones.centro:
I hope the head-to-head debate between Sánchez and Feijóo serves a purpose beyond managing electoral expectations. I want to hear verifiable proposals on housing, funding for public services and institutional renewal, not just strategies to mobilise each political camp. Corruption deserves debate and, where appropriate, independent investigation; political negotiation also requires transparency and respect for shared rules.

I am concerned that fewer people vote in lower-income neighbourhoods. It is not enough to call for participation: people must be given reasons to trust that politics can improve everyday life. That requires lasting agreements, effective public investment and a private sector capable of creating jobs and expanding the supply of housing. Tax cuts, meanwhile, must be assessed alongside their cost to social welfare. I prefer gradual, funded reforms to promises that nobody explains how they will sustain.
